section.title: What is Wi-Fi?
section.p: is a wireless technology that allows devices such as laptops, smartphones, tablets, printers, and smart TVs to connect to a network and access the Internet without using cables. Wi‑Fi uses radio waves to transmit data between devices and a wireless router or access point.

section.title: How Wi-Fi Communicates
section.p: A wireless broadcasts a Wi-Fi signal within a coverage area. Devices that are within range can detect the wireless network and request a connection.
After successful authentication, the router exchanges data with the connected devices and forwards Internet traffic through the or optical network terminal (ONT).

section.title: Wi-Fi Network Name
section.p: Every Wi-Fi network has a unique name called a Service Set Identifier (SSID). Users select the SSID when they connect a device to a wireless network.
